top_strength: Excellent, disciplined discovery on a genuinely complicated three-stop move — she pinned down every address with zip, both parking situations, floor counts, the freight elevator and move-in bay, and even the walk distance from the elevator to the apartment door, then read the whole itemized item list back before quoting. The $936-$1,144 / 4.5-5.5 hour estimate is internally consistent with the $104/hr/mover rate and defensible for the scope described.
coaching_note: This call had the single clearest Save Your Ass opening of any call this week and Jeline walked right past it. The customer literally said 'I'm really only hiring movers for the big pieces of furniture' and 'I also have some things that I'll take from Brighton to Majestic' — she is already prep-minded and cost-conscious. That is the exact moment to run the prep speech: consolidate loose drawer items, pull photos off the walls, box up the small stuff, take a carload yourself, and it shortens the move and lowers the bill. On a 4.5-5.5 hour three-stop job, that speech is worth real dollars to the customer and real time to the crew. Add it right after the estimate, before the booking, and close it with 'does that make sense?'
phone_presence_notes: Consistently polite and thankful with a warm farewell, but transactional throughout — heavy 'Mm-hmm' filler in place of real acknowledgment, no empathy or affirmation language, and she let the customer's repeat-customer mention and roommate clarification pass without any rapport response.
audio_review_reason: Transcript is heavily garbled in the rep's pricing block ('no heat and fees', 'no terrible fees', 'not daily contracted or Chris', 'Just cancel' where 'Kendall' is likely intended), so the clarity/pace deduction in Section 9 and the customer-name-use credit in Section 8 both need audio confirmation.
